flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for gross profit?
What is the formula for net profit?
What is the formula for gross profit margin?
What is the formula for net profit margin?
What is the formula for the average rate of return?
What does a business keep from every £1 of sales at an 8% net profit margin?
What is the gross profit when a shop sells 400 hoodies at £28 each and each hoodie costs £15?
What is EuroParts' net profit when gross profit is £18,020 and operating expenses are £14,450?
What is the gross profit margin when gross profit is £4,810 and sales revenue is £18,500?
What is the net profit margin when net profit is £25m and sales revenue is £435m?
What is the average rate of return on a £90m project that earns £2,250m of profit over 40 years?
What does cost of sales include?
flashcard_questions.a: The direct costs of making or buying the products a business sells.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is net profit often called the most important profit figure?
flashcard_questions.a: It is the money actually left once every cost has been paid.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can a business have a high gross profit margin but a low net profit margin?
flashcard_questions.a: Its operating costs are very high.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main weakness of judging an investment by its average rate of return?
flashcard_questions.a: It relies on predicted profits, which may turn out to be inaccurate.

notes: 15 cards: 5 formula cards quoted exactly as the lesson states them, 5 one-step calculations using the lesson's own figures (hoodies, EuroParts, £18,500 GPM, £435m NPM, Jacksons Project B), 1 interpretation card on what an 8% NPM means per £1, 2 term→definition, 2 evaluation facts (net profit importance, ARR weakness). Dropped 'sales revenue' and 'operating costs' as standalone definition cards — they appear inside the formula cards and would interfere.
